summary: Bunkyo Aoki worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Ryukoku University and under Kozui Otani (~1908–1914), later serving as a Tibetan language lecturer at the University of Tokyo from 1951, succeeding Tokan Tada.

Bunsaku Kurata was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology who studied at Aoyama Gakuin and Waseda universities. He held posts at the Tokyo National Museum, the National Commission for the Protection of Cultural Properties, and served as Director of Nara National Museum (1975).

Bunyiu Nanjio was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology who studied at Takakura Gakuryo, Otani University, and Oxford under Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He held posts at the University of Tokyo and served as director of Otani University.

Bunzaburo Matsumoto specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, studying at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Rikkyo University, the First Higher School, and Kyoto University, where he also served as president (1908–1915), later directing the Academy of Oriental Culture, Kyoto Institute.

Burchard Brentjes was an archaeologist and historian of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg under Heinz Adolf Mode (~1948–1954), later working there (~1954–1989) and succeeding Mode in 1978.
Burkhard Quessel is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Hamburg, where he was a member (attested 1997). He later served as a curator at the British Library (attested 2002–2012).
Burton Stein was a historian and Indologist. He held academic posts at the University of Hawaiʻi from approximately 1966 to 1986 and at SOAS University of London from approximately 1986 to 1996.

Burton Watson was a scholar of Sinology and Japanology who studied at Columbia University under William Theodore de Bary and at Kyoto University. He taught English at Doshisha University and held professorships at Columbia University and Stanford University.

Byambyn Rinchen was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the Leningrad Orient Institute (~1924–1927) and Eötvös Loránd University (1956), and held a post at the National University of Mongolia.
Byung-gon Kim is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He studied at Rissho University (attested 2007) and held a post as professor, dean, and institute director at Minobusan University (attested 2026).

C. D. Sebastian specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Banaras Hindu University, studied under Paul Williams, Gavin D'Costa, Ashok Kumar Chatterjee, and Abhimanyu Singh, and became Professor of Indian Philosophy at IIT Bombay (attested 2016).

C. M. Naim was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1959–1961) and served as a faculty member and Professor Emeritus at the University of Chicago (~1961–2001).

C. Pierce Salguero is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Virginia and Johns Hopkins University, later holding posts at Pennsylvania State University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Penn State Abington (~2011).
C. R. Krishnamacharlu was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Madras Christian College and completed his university degree at Pachaiyappa's College.
C. S. Srinivasachari was a historian and Indologist who held posts as a professor at Pachaiyappa's College and at Annamalai University (attested 1932–1933).
C. Scott Littleton was a scholar of linguistics, Japanology, and Indology. He studied at the University of California, Los Angeles from approximately 1955 to 1964, working under Jaan Puhvel.

C. W. Huntington, Jr. specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan (~1980–1986) under Luis O. Gómez and Madhav M. Deshpande, and served as a professor at Hartwick College (~1992–2020).
Caixi Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies who pursued a PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the doctoral supervision of Wadinagala Pannaloka (attested 2026).

Calambur Sivaramamurti was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Presidency University under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He held curatorial and leadership positions at the Government Museum in Chennai, the Indian Museum, the Archaeological Survey of India, and the National Museum, New Delhi.

Calvert Watkins worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Harvard, the EPHE, and DIAS, later serving as professor of linguistics and classics at Harvard (1959–2003) and distinguished professor in residence at UCLA (2003–2013).
